desc:
Extension onboarding and upgrade flow work from Ecom Swift LLC helps new installs become active users, with a clear welcome, a better popup call to action, an honest upgrade prompt and simple event counts.

## Why do people install an extension and never use it?

People install an extension and leave it unused because they do not know what to do next. The toolbar icon is small, the popup may be empty on first open and nothing explains the first useful step. Within a minute the user forgets why they installed it.

An extension onboarding and upgrade flow fixes that minute. It shows the next action, proves the value quickly and only then mentions a paid plan. For extension owners, this is often the cheapest improvement available, since it works on the installs you already have.

## How a better first run improves results

Installs are only the start. What matters is how many users complete a first success, return later, leave a good rating and, where you charge, upgrade. Each of these steps depends on the one before it.

A clear first screen reduces confusion. A first success builds confidence. Asking for a rating or an upgrade right after that success feels fair, while asking at install feels pushy. Counting events at each step shows where people stop, so you improve the right screen instead of guessing. The outcome depends on your product, your audience and your traffic, so we describe the work and what it improves rather than promising a number.

## What a good onboarding and upgrade flow includes

- A welcome page that opens once after install and states the main benefit in one line.
- A short step-by-step guide that ends with the user doing the real task.
- A popup headline and button written in plain, specific words.
- Empty states that tell the user what to do instead of showing a blank box.
- An upgrade prompt shown after a success, with the paid benefits listed honestly.
- A clear way to dismiss any prompt without penalty.
- A rating request placed after a good moment, not during a task.
- An uninstall page that asks why the person left.
- Event counts for each step, collected without personal details.

## What we do

We start by installing your extension as a first-time user and recording where we hesitate. Then we rewrite the popup text, build the welcome flow and place prompts at moments that fit the user's progress. We add simple event counts so each step can be measured, and we explain what is counted so your privacy answers stay accurate.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages add depth. Basic gives you a welcome screen and a sharper call to action. Standard builds a guided flow with an upgrade prompt, helpful empty states and step counts. Premium adds two onboarding versions to compare, a rating prompt, an uninstall feedback page and a results sheet.

Every prompt follows the store's rules about not misleading or pressuring users.

## Do and avoid with upgrade prompts

**Do:**
- Show the paid benefit in terms of the task the user just finished.
- Let people close a prompt and not see it again for a while.
- Write buttons as verbs: Save page, Start tour, See plans.
- Keep one main action per screen.
- Compare one change at a time so you know what worked.

**Avoid:**
- Blocking the free feature behind a pop-up right after install.
- Using fake countdowns or invented scarcity.
- Collecting identifiers you do not need to count a step.
- Asking for a review before the user has had any value.
- Hiding the close button or the free option.

## Who this is for

It suits an extension with steady installs but few daily users. It suits an owner who added a paid plan and sees few upgrades. And it suits a team that just redesigned the product and wants new users to understand it.

## What we need from you

Send the extension code or a test build, the store link and your main goal: more use, more upgrades or more reviews. Tell us how you charge, if you do, and which payment or licence tool you use. You do not need payments set up to benefit from the onboarding work.

We never ask for passwords. We work from your code or a shared repository invite, and we send a short checklist after you order.
